text: APPROVE: The guard clauses keep the original order and short-circuiting, so behaviour is the same. The extracted `DisabledEntryKey` returns `string?` and the caller null-checks it, so there's no new nullable warning. Splitting the nested `if` chain out of the loop clearly drops the method's complexity below 15. One thing I couldn't confirm from the diff: the unchanged lines after the loop's guards must not use the removed `entry` local, or the build would fail.
